# OROLABIAL HERPES

---

References:

- Mandell chapter: Herpes simplex virus
- Sanford keyword: Herpes simplex
- Up-To-Date article: Treatment of herpes simplex virus type 1 infection in immunocompetent patients
Therapy:
## Inpatient

### Immunocompetent patients

---

Antiviral therapy is not beneficial after formation of vesicles. However, when started as soon as prodromal symptoms of burning or tingling occur, antivirals reduce duration of pain and lesions.
Acyclovir 400 mg PO q8h for 5 days ($) [R]

---

### Immunocompromised patients

---

Immunocompromised patients in whom herpes simplex infections can be more severe include: patients with HIV infection, organ transplant recipients, patients undergoing chemotherapy, malnourished patients, and those with compromised skin integrity.

## Outpatient

Guidance

---

Acyclovir 400 mg PO TID for 5 days ($) [R]
Valacyclovir 2 gm BID for 1 day ($) [R]

### Treatment for mild to moderate disease

Acyclovir 400 mg PO TID for 7-14 days($) [R]
Valacyclovir 1 gm BID for 7-14 days ($) [R]

---

Acyclovir 400 mg PO BID ($) [R]
Valacyclovir 500 mg PO QDay ($) [R]

### Alternative

Valacyclovir 2 gm q12h for 1 day ($) [R]

Treatment for mild to moderate disease

Acyclovir 400 mg PO q8h for 7-14 days($) [R]
< OR >
Valacyclovir 1 gm q12h for 7-14 days ($) [R]

### Treatment for severe disease

Acyclovir 5 mg/kg IV q8h for 7-14 days ($$) [R]

### Chronic suppressive therapy

Indicated for patients with greater than 6 recurrences or severe recurrences, immunocompromised patients or as adjunct to prevent transmission. Suppressive therapy is optional, and some patients may find episodic treatment more convenient. Patients should be reassessed every few years to evaluate if chronic suppressive therapy is still necessary.
Acyclovir 400 mg PO q12h ($) [R]
< OR >
Valacyclovir 500 mg PO Q24h ($) [R]
